GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2019-10-14T05:12:59Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: `dotnet publish` produces executable specific to OS it's executed on
Description: I noticed that Windows hosting the `dotnet publish` gets an EXE file, while Linux (Ubuntu) gets an extensionless executable file named by the assembly. Under assumption that produced DLL and json-config files are actually exactly the same (regardless of where this process executes), shouldn't the process produce entrypoint binaries for all supported operating systems [at the same time]? Maybe I'm not noticing that the behavior that I'm after is actually present? The behavior that I'm noticing might complicate the build-process in certain scenarios. I just wanted to bring it to your attention. Thanks.

llm_response:
CATEGORY: 1
REASONING: This issue is discussing the behavior of `dotnet publish` producing different executable formats depending on the OS where the command is run (Windows produces .exe files, Linux produces extensionless executables). This is a conceptual question about how the .NET build system works, not a bug that needs to be reproduced through building code. The user is asking whether the tool should produce executables for all supported operating systems simultaneously, regardless of the build platform. 

This can be verified by explaining the expected behavior of the dotnet CLI tools without needing to set up a build environment. The answer would involve explaining that this is the designed behavior of the dotnet publish command, which by default targets the current platform unless specified otherwise through runtime identifiers (RIDs). No actual code execution or build environment is needed to verify this explanation.
